1.e4 e5 2.d3 Nf6 3.f4.strategy: Attacks the e5-pawn, which no black piece defends yet, and aims for an open f-file. It loosens the king's side before any piece is out, and e4 is held only by the d-pawn, so Black can answer with active play and equalise comfortably.

1.e4 e5 2.d3 Nf6 3.f4 Bc5.strategy: Leaves e5 en prise on purpose and hits the g1 knight along the diagonal the f-pawn has opened. If White takes, ...Nxe4 sacrifices the knight for a check on h4 after dxe4. The idea is speculative: Black is a pawn down at once and needs the follow-up to work.
1.e4 e5 2.d3 Nf6 3.f4 Bc5.name: King's Pawn Game: Clam Variation, Radisch Gambit
